gaps.description: Existing low-resource MT benchmarks rarely include truly low-resource African or Oceanic languages with under 10k parallel sentences. Transfer methods are validated on medium-resource pairs, leaving their effectiveness on the lowest-resource settings unmeasured.
gaps.potential_impact: Robust benchmarks for the lowest-resource languages would expose where cross-lingual transfer actually breaks and guide targeted data collection.
gaps.title: Lack of truly low-resource African and Oceanic language pairs in MT benchmarks

gaps.description: Morpheme-aware metrics have been proposed but never validated on polysynthetic languages where a single word encodes a full clause. It is unknown whether such metrics correlate with human fluency judgments in these settings.
gaps.potential_impact: Validated morpheme-aware metrics would make MT evaluation trustworthy for the languages where it currently fails most.
gaps.title: Morpheme-aware evaluation metrics are unvalidated for polysynthetic languages

papers.abstract: We survey benchmarks for low-resource machine translation, covering 40 language pairs and evaluating data scarcity, tokenization, and evaluation metric reliability. We find that standard BLEU scores under-report quality for morphologically rich languages and that few benchmarks include truly low-resource African or Oceanic languages.
papers.title: A Survey of Low-Resource Machine Translation Benchmarks

papers.abstract: Cross-lingual transfer from multilingual encoders has advanced for medium-resource languages but struggles for endangered languages with minimal monolingual data. We review transfer techniques and identify open problems in script normalization, code-switching, and dialect continua.
papers.title: Cross-Lingual Transfer for Endangered Languages: A Review

papers.abstract: Standard MT evaluation metrics assume whitespace tokenization and fail on morphologically rich, agglutinative languages. We propose morpheme-aware metrics and show that chrF under-estimates fluency for polysynthetic languages.
papers.title: Evaluation Metrics for Morphologically Rich Languages

research_question: How can cross-lingual transfer and evaluation be made reliable for truly low-resource languages?
